item: CWC water-level data (Naraj, Alipingal, Nimapara + 55 more stations)
detail: Real manual hourly gauge readings, 2021-2025, read directly from the supplied CWC CSV.
Downloaded by user from USGS EarthExplorer, integrity/CRS/resolution/coverage independently verified.
Manifest, annotation, calibration, noise and RFI files all verified genuine and matching this exact product.
Manifest, annotation, and measurement pixel data verified genuine for this exact product.
Government-sourced flood extent polygons, spatially confirmed to intersect the Naraj AOI.

Radiometric calibration to sigma0 IS complete for both 6-Aug and 18-Aug (verified product-specific LUTs). Noise (NESZ) subtraction was additionally demonstrated for 6-Aug, but the 18-Aug noise LUT is no longer available (lost to a filename collision after verification). The candidate mask uses the consistent, non-noise-corrected pair for both dates rather than mixing processing levels.

The vertical reference behind the CWC gauge fields (RL_of_zeroGauge, MeanSeaLevel) has not been reconciled with the SRTM DEM's EGM96 datum. No gauge reading is converted to an absolute terrain elevation anywhere in this prototype -- the Terrain Scenario tab uses relative elevation only.

A candidate flood mask HAS been produced (18-Aug), using calibrated, geocoded, co-registered Sentinel-1 VV+VH change detection (>=3dB drop in both bands, spatially filtered). Validated against the verified NDEM 18-Aug reference within the SAR valid-coverage area: IoU=0.14, Precision=0.15, Recall=0.66, F1=0.24. These are real, calculated prototype-stage metrics, not a validated operational accuracy figure -- precision is low, meaning the candidate mask currently over-detects (see Data & Methodology for why). Noise (NESZ) correction was successfully demonstrated for 6-Aug but could not be applied consistently to 18-Aug in this pass (LUT file no longer available -- see SAR_FLOOD_DETECTION_REPORT.md); the mask therefore uses the non-noise-corrected pair for methodological consistency between dates.

SAR rasters are geocoded using a GCP-based thin-plate-spline warp (GDAL), not full SAR range-Doppler terrain correction -- this environment has no SAR-specific processing toolkit (e.g. ESA SNAP). A reasonable approximation given the AOI's flat terrain, but not verified to true RTC accuracy.

The 6-Aug/18-Aug same-orbit pair covers ~65% of the defined AOI. SAR-based analysis (change detection, candidate mask) is restricted to this valid-coverage area; the remaining ~35% is shown as 'no SAR coverage', never treated as 'not flooded'.

A literature-consistent starting threshold, not an optimized or validated value for this site. A full sensitivity analysis (1-6 dB) is available in SAR_FLOOD_DETECTION_REPORT.md, showing candidate area ranges from 220 km2 (1dB) down to 26 km2 (6dB).
